root_cause.text: hid_post_reset() in the usbhid reset path allocated the HID report descriptor buffer with GFP_KERNEL even though it runs during USB/block I/O error handling, allowing memory reclaim to trigger block I/O and deadlock against the device-reset mutex.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, GFP_NOIO)` in `drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-core.c`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `hid_pre_reset()`/`hid_post_reset()` are executed in block I/O error handling where allocations must not do block I/O because they can deadlock on the mutex held while resetting the device.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use GFP_NOIO instead of GFP_KERNEL when allocating the HID report descriptor during post-reset handling to avoid unsafe I/O-related memory reclaim in reset context.
intent_record.what: The memory allocation flag in hid_post_reset() was changed from GFP_KERNEL to GFP_NOIO in the kmalloc(hid->dev_rsize, ...) call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the buffer allocation for the HID report descriptor after a USB reset will avoid initiating filesystem or other I/O-related reclaim paths, reducing the risk of blocking or reentrancy issues in this reset handling context while still allocating the same sized buffer.

grouping_result.intent: Use GFP_NOIO instead of GFP_KERNEL when allocating the HID report descriptor during post-reset handling to avoid unsafe I/O-related memory reclaim in reset context.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it replaces GFP_KERNEL with GFP_NOIO for HID report descriptor allocation in hid_post_reset(), preventing memory reclaim from initiating I/O during reset/error-handling context and avoiding the deadlock.

candidates.rationale: This allocation occurs in hid_post_reset() during USB/block I/O error handling reset context. Using GFP_KERNEL permits memory reclaim that may initiate block I/O, which can deadlock against the device-reset mutex. The vulnerable root cause is specifically the unsafe GFP_KERNEL allocation flag here.

vuln_statements.explanation: In hid_post_reset(), this allocation used GFP_KERNEL while running in USB/block I/O error-handling reset context. GFP_KERNEL may enter memory reclaim and trigger block I/O, which can deadlock against the device-reset mutex. The fix intent explicitly identifies replacing this flag with GFP_NOIO.
